full_text_en:
China Shipping Industry (Jiangsu) Co., Ltd. v. China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Yangzhou Central Branch and China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. — dispute over marine insurance contract

Ruling Summary

A vessel under construction, since it has not yet passed various technical inspections and undergone formal registration procedures, can hardly constitute a "vessel" within the meaning of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Maritime Code), and is even less qualified to engage in vessel operation activities. Therefore, the trial navigation of a vessel under construction is merely an activity related to "ship construction," rather than an activity directly related to "ship operation" as listed in Article 207, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Maritime Code. Consequently, the claim for damages arising therefrom does not constitute a limited claim. Hence, when an accident occurs during the trial navigation of a vessel under construction, causing personal injury or property damage to others, the person liable cannot enjoy the limitation of liability for maritime claims.

Plaintiff: China Shipping Industry (Jiangsu) Co., Ltd., domicile: Hanzhong Road, Gulou District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal representative: Lin Jianqing, chairman of the company.

Defendant: China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Yangzhou Central Branch, domicile: Wenchang Middle Road, Guangling District, Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Person in charge: Wu Hua, general manager of the branch.

Defendant: China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd., domicile: Yincheng Middle Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.
Legal representative: Wu Zongmin, chairman and general manager of the company.

Plaintiff China Shipping Industry (Jiangsu) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Shipping Industry) filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Maritime Court against defendant China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Yangzhou Central Branch (hereinafter referred to as Taibao Yangzhou Company) and defendant China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taibao Company) concerning a dispute over a marine insurance contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations

On November 14, 2008, the plaintiff insured a bulk carrier under construction with hull number CIS57300-04 (hereinafter referred to as the "Anmin Mountain" vessel) with the defendant Taibao Yangzhou Company under a ship construction insurance policy, and paid a premium of RMB 448,000. On the same day, Taibao Yangzhou Company issued Ship Construction Insurance Policy No. ANAJK0123108B000008N, with a sum insured of RMB 280,000,000. The scope of insurance coverage included the liability of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel for compensation for property loss and personal injury to third parties arising from collisions and contacts during trial navigation. On July 9, 2009, during the trial navigation of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel from Jiangdu, Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province to the sea area of Huanshan Island, Zhejiang Province, while passing through the Fujiangsha South Waterway of Zhangjiagang, the vessel lost power and went out of control, first contacting the wharf of Zhangjiagang Donghua Energy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Donghua Company), and then colliding with the vessel "Huahang Mingrui No. 16." This accident caused damage to the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, the sinking of the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16," partial collapse of the Donghua Company wharf, and the drowning death of one wharf worker. The Zhangjiagang Maritime Safety Administration issued an accident investigation conclusion on October 25, 2009, determining that the "Anmin Mountain" vessel bore full responsibility for the accident. After the accident, the plaintiff paid a total of RMB 297,033,828 for costs including on-site emergency repair and waterway dredging fees, mooring and unmooring fees for the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, transportation fees, berthing fees, tugboat fees, salvage fees for the sunken "Huahang Mingrui No. 16," repair fees for the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, compensation for the deceased, compensation for the loss of the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16," wharf wreck removal fees, navigation mark installation fees, wharf reconstruction fees, wharf facility and pipeline reconstruction fees, wharf design fees, wharf supervision fees, compensation for wharf delay operation losses, appraisal fees, etc. The plaintiff notified Taibao Yangzhou Company on the same day of the accident, requesting it to conduct survey and loss assessment. The plaintiff subsequently negotiated with Taibao Yangzhou Company regarding insurance claims on multiple occasions, but Taibao Yangzhou Company has only paid RMB 60,000,000 in insurance proceeds to date. The plaintiff contends that the losses and liabilities arising from the above accident fall within the scope of the insurer's liability, and Taibao Yangzhou Company should pay the insurance proceeds. However, Taibao Yangzhou Company has failed to fully perform its obligations under the insurance contract, causing damage to the plaintiff's interests. Since Taibao Yangzhou Company is a branch of defendant Taibao Company, Taibao Company should bear joint and several liability for the above economic losses of the plaintiff. The plaintiff requests judgment: 1. Order the two defendants to jointly and severally pay the plaintiff insurance proceeds of RMB 237,033,828 and interest losses (interest on RMB 90,373,828 from June 29, 2011, to the effective date of the judgment; interest on RMB 141,969,500 from November 14, 2011, to the effective date of the judgment; interest on RMB 4,690,500 from January 9, 2012, to the effective date of the judgment; all calculated at the one-year loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China); 2. The two defendants jointly bear the court acceptance fee for this case.

The plaintiff China Shipping Industry submitted the following evidence:

1. Ship construction insurance policy, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry and the defendant Taibao Yangzhou Company concluded a legal and valid insurance contract.
2. Insurance premium invoice and bank payment receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid the insurance premium as agreed.
3. Conclusion of investigation on inland river traffic accident, to prove that the "Anmin Mountain" vessel bore full responsibility for the insured accident.
4. Sunken vessel salvage contract, invoice, and bank payment receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid salvage fees of RMB 990,000 for the sunken vessel.
5. Emergency rescue, salvage, and relocation agreement, invoice, and bank payment receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid on-site emergency repair and waterway dredging fees of RMB 4,137,288, and mooring/unmooring fees, transportation fees, and berthing fees of RMB 682,812.
6. Towage agreement, invoice, and bank payment receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid tugboat fees of RMB 780,000.
7. Mediation agreement and receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid compensation of RMB 580,000 to the family of the deceased.
8. Settlement agreement, receipt, and bank payment receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid compensation of RMB 5,910,000 to the owner of the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16" vessel.
9. Ship repair contract, receipt, and invoice, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid repair fees of RMB 10,642,031 for the "Anmin Mountain" vessel.
10. Wharf salvage and demolition project contract, notarized document, bank payment receipt, and invoice, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid wharf wreck removal fees of RMB 6,480,000.
11. Agreement and bank payment receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry reached an agreement with Donghua Company on compensation matters such as wharf wreck removal and reconstruction, and paid an aggregate pre-payment of RMB 118,480,000.
12. Consulting service engagement letter, invoice, and consulting report, to prove that Donghua Company paid consulting fees of RMB 600,000 to its engaged Jiangsu Fuhua Certified Public Accountants.
13. Engagement letter, invoice, bank payment receipt, and report, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid appraisal fees of RMB 700,000 to its engaged Shanghai Hongda Dongya Certified Public Accountants.
14. Agreement and bank payment receipt, to prove that based on the appraisal reports of the accounting firms engaged respectively by the parties, the plaintiff China Shipping Industry and Donghua Company determined that the wharf delay operation period for Donghua Company was 24 months, with total losses of RMB 218,342,197, and Donghua Company confirmed on November 14, 2011, that it had received RMB 146,660,000.
15. Bank payment receipt, to prove that the plaintiff China Shipping Industry made an additional payment of RMB 4,690,500 for delay operation losses on January 9, 2012.

Defendant Taibao Yangzhou Company's Defense

1. Some of the losses claimed by the plaintiff China Shipping Industry are unreasonable; the reasonable amount for repair fees of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel should be RMB 6,092,011; the plaintiff's claimed appraisal fee of RMB 1,300,000 includes fees for two appraisal firms, and Taibao Yangzhou Company does not accept the RMB 600,000 portion. 2. The sum insured under the policy is RMB 280,000,000, and the contract also stipulates a deductible of RMB 100,000 per accident; even if the insurer is liable, the liability should be limited to the sum insured and the deductible should be applied. 3. As the owner of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, the plaintiff is entitled to limitation of liability for maritime claims under the law; however, the plaintiff did not raise the issue of limitation of liability for maritime claims in its negotiations with Donghua Company, to which Taibao Yangzhou Company objects. 4. Taibao Yangzhou Company did not delay payment in this case and should not bear interest losses; the plaintiff's claim for interest calculated at the loan interest rate is unfounded and should be calculated at the one-year deposit interest rate.

Defendant Taibao Company's Defense

The policy in question was issued by defendant Taibao Yangzhou Company. Although Taibao Yangzhou Company is a branch of Taibao Company, it has independent litigation status under the law. Therefore, Taibao Company should not bear compensation liability to the plaintiff China Shipping Industry in this case. Taibao Company otherwise agrees with the defense of Taibao Yangzhou Company.

The two defendants jointly submitted the following evidence:

Survey report No. CS-YZ-TB-09309 issued by Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors and Adjusters Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuezhi Company), to prove the reasonable amount of losses from the accident in question.

The Shanghai Maritime Court conducted cross-examination in accordance with the law. During the trial, defendants Taibao Yangzhou Company and Taibao Company acknowledged the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the plaintiff's evidence items 1–8, 10, 11, and 13–15. They acknowledged the authenticity of evidence item 9 but asserted that the amount of the fees was unreasonable, and that according to the estimate of the survey company engaged by the two defendants, the reasonable repair costs were RMB 6,092,011. They did not acknowledge the authenticity of evidence item 12 because the plaintiff did not provide the original payment voucher and the payer was not the plaintiff. The plaintiff acknowledged the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the survey report submitted by the two defendants.

Facts Found by the Shanghai Maritime Court at First Instance

On November 14, 2008, the plaintiff China Shipping Industry insured a bulk carrier under construction with hull number CIS57300-04 (later named the "Anmin Mountain" vessel) with the defendant Taibao Yangzhou Company under a ship construction insurance policy. On the same day, Taibao Yangzhou Company issued Ship Construction Insurance Policy No. ANAJK0123108B000008N. The policy stated: the plaintiff is the contractor under the construction contract and the insured; the contract number and hull number of the insured vessel are CIS57300-04; the place of construction is the plaintiff's shipyard and its subcontractors; the trial navigation area is the Yangtze River and East China Sea waters within a radius of 500 nautical miles centered on Shanghai; the insurance period is from 00:00 hours on November 15, 2008, to 24:00 hours on September 30, 2009; the total insured value and total sum insured are both RMB 280,000,000; the premium rate is 0.16%; the premium is RMB 448,000; the absolute deductible per accident is RMB 100,000; and the insurance clauses are the Ship Construction Insurance Clauses. In addition to the insurance policy, the insurance contract concluded between the plaintiff and Taibao Yangzhou Company also includes the "Ship Construction Insurance Clauses" and "Special Agreements on Ship Construction Insurance." According to the provisions of the above insurance contract, the scope of the insurer's liability includes: losses and expenses caused by natural disasters or accidents to the insured vessel during construction, trial navigation, and delivery at the shipyard; losses and expenses caused by negligence, error, or lack of experience of workers, technicians, master, crew, and pilots; after a collision accident, compensation liability legally borne by the insured vessel for damage to the collided vessel and its cargo, floating objects, docks, wharves, or other fixed structures, and for loss of and loss of use thereof, as well as salvage costs, general average, and salvage expenses, provided that such liability is limited to the sum insured of the insured vessel; and expenses for removing the wreck of the insured vessel and liability for personal injury to third parties arising from a collision accident suffered by the insured vessel, provided that such liability is limited to the sum insured of the insured vessel; and so on. In addition, the insurance contract also agreed that after the occurrence of an insured event, if it is determined through investigation that the loss is caused by an insured accident, the insurer shall, within four weeks after the occurrence of the accident, first pay the actual loss amount to the account designated by the plaintiff. On December 5, 2008, the plaintiff paid the insurance premium of RMB 448,000 to Taibao Yangzhou Branch.

At 1007 hours on July 9, 2009, the "Anmin Mountain" vessel departed from the plaintiff China Shipping Industry's Jiangdu shipyard wharf for trial navigation to the sea area of Huanshan Island, Zhejiang Province. At 1443 hours on the same day, while the "Anmin Mountain" vessel was passing through the Fujiangsha South Waterway of the Yangtze River and overtaking the vessel "Huahang Mingrui No. 16," near the waters of the #48 black buoy of the Yangtze River, a generator failure on the vessel caused a complete loss of power, resulting in loss of control of the main engine and steering gear, causing the vessel to go out of control. At 1446 hours, the "Anmin Mountain" vessel contacted the Donghua Company wharf. At 1448 hours, the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16," which was descending on the starboard quarter of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, was unable to avoid a collision and collided with the stern rudder blade of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel. The accident caused damage to the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, the sinking of the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16," partial collapse of the Donghua Company wharf, and the drowning death of one wharf worker. On October 25, 2009, the Zhangjiagang Maritime Safety Administration of the People's Republic of China issued an accident investigation conclusion, determining that the accident was caused by the loss of power, main engine, and steering gear of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, resulting in the vessel going out of control; the "Anmin Mountain" vessel bore full responsibility for the accident, and the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16" and Donghua Company were not liable.

To handle the aftermath of the accident, during the period from July 14, 2009, to August 25, 2009, the plaintiff China Shipping Industry paid: on-site rescue fees of RMB 4,137,288 and berthing fees of RMB 682,812 to Zhangjiagang Free Trade Zone Gangtong Ship Service Co., Ltd.; towage fees of RMB 780,000 to Jiangyin Chenggang Tugboat Shipping Co., Ltd.; compensation for losses of RMB 5,910,000 to Wang Huili, owner of the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16"; salvage fees of RMB 990,000 for the sunken vessel to Yancheng Wenqiang Dredging and Salvage Co., Ltd. (the total salvage price was RMB 1,945,000, and the wreck of the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16" was valued at RMB 955,000, which was used to offset the salvage fees, so the plaintiff actually paid RMB 990,000); and compensation of RMB 580,000 to the family of the deceased Sun Longhua. The above expenses totaled RMB 13,080,100. On July 25, 2009, the plaintiff entered into a ship repair contract with China Shipping Industry Co., Ltd. for the "Anmin Mountain" vessel, agreeing on a repair cost of RMB 10,642,031, with the actual repair work to be carried out by China Shipping Industry (Shanghai Changxing) Co., Ltd. The plaintiff and Donghua Company entered into four agreements on July 9, 2009, December 10, 2009, June 20, 2010, and June 13, 2011, regarding the cleaning and reconstruction of the damaged wharf, determination of delay operation losses, and compensation plans. They respectively engaged Shanghai Hongda Dongya Certified Public Accountants and Jiangsu Fuhua Certified Public Accountants to assess the delay operation losses of the damaged wharf. Both accounting firms' appraisal reports determined that Donghua Company's marginal profit loss related to the damaged wharf was RMB 299,098.90 per day. Based on the conclusions of the appraisal reports, the plaintiff and Donghua Company confirmed that Donghua Company's operating loss period due to the wharf collision was 24 months, with total losses of RMB 218,342,197. On June 10, 2011, the plaintiff paid appraisal fees of RMB 700,000 to Shanghai Hongda Dongya Certified Public Accountants it had engaged. Pursuant to the agreements with Donghua Company, the plaintiff paid Donghua Company: on August 10, 2009, RMB 16,000,000; on August 19, 2009, RMB 6,480,000; on December 28, 2009, RMB 30,000,000; on July 16, 2010, RMB 30,000,000; on June 29, 2011, RMB 36,000,000; on November 14, 2011, RMB 141,969,500; and on January 9, 2012, RMB 4,690,500, for a total of RMB 265,140,000 paid to Donghua Company.

After the accident occurred, the plaintiff China Shipping Industry promptly notified defendant Taibao Yangzhou Company. On July 12, 2009, Yuezhi Company, commissioned by Taibao Yangzhou Company, dispatched surveyors to the site to conduct survey and loss assessment. On December 5, 2011, Yuezhi Company issued Survey Report No. CS-YZ-TB-09309, assessing the scope and extent of damage to the vessel and wharf, as well as various losses resulting from the accident. In the report, Yuezhi Company acknowledged all fees paid by the plaintiff totaling RMB 13,080,100, including on-site rescue fees, berthing fees, towage fees, compensation for the loss of the "Huahang Mingrui No. 16," salvage fees for the sunken vessel, and compensation for the deceased; it determined that the reasonable amount for repair fees of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel was RMB 6,092,011; it determined that the costs for cleaning and reconstruction of the damaged wharf included: salvage and cleaning fees for the wharf wreck of RMB 4,480,000 (the plaintiff paid Donghua Company RMB 6,480,000 for wharf wreck salvage and cleaning, but the proceeds from disposing of the wharf wreck were RMB 2,000,000; after deducting this amount, the wharf wreck salvage and cleaning fees should be RMB 4,480,000), wharf reconstruction fees of RMB 18,898,300, wharf facility and pipeline reconstruction fees of RMB 26,930,600, wharf design fees of RMB 2,291,500, wharf supervision fees of RMB 916,600, and navigation mark installation fees of RMB 152,500; and it considered Donghua Company's wharf delay operation losses of RMB 218,342,197 to be reasonable. The plaintiff acknowledged the conclusions of the Yuezhi Company appraisal report and confirmed that the actual amounts paid for wharf reconstruction fees were RMB 17,858,500 and for wharf facility and pipeline reconstruction fees were RMB 20,498,900.

Defendant Taibao Yangzhou Company paid a total of RMB 60,000,000 to the plaintiff China Shipping Industry in two installments, on August 19, 2009, and January 20, 2010. Taibao Yangzhou Company is a branch of Taibao Company that is established and holds a business license.

Separately, it was found that before the trial navigation, the "Anmin Mountain" vessel had applied to the Yangzhou Maritime Safety Administration of the People's Republic of China for issuance of the "Certificate of Nationality for Ships of the People's Republic of China" and the "Certificate of Minimum Safe Manning (Coastal Vessel)," and had obtained a "Certificate of Trial Navigation for Vessels" issued by the China Classification Society. According to the above certificates, the plaintiff China Shipping Industry was the operator of the "Anmin Mountain" vessel during the trial navigation period, and the vessel's gross tonnage was 33,511 tons.

During the trial of this case, the plaintiff Zhonghai Industry and the two defendants confirmed: the appraisal fee paid by the plaintiff to Shanghai Hongda East Asia Certified Public Accountants was not a cost for inspecting and evaluating the nature and extent of the insured accident, but rather a loss arising from the accident; according to the agreement between the plaintiff and Tai Bao Yangzhou Company, the absolute deductible of RMB 100,000 in the insurance contract shall be deducted from the total insured amount of RMB 280,000,000 regardless of whether the total loss exceeds the insured amount. At the same time, the plaintiff clarified its claim for interest losses: it divided the interest losses on the amounts payable by the two defendants into three time periods, among which RMB 141,969,500 and RMB 4,690,500 were the last two payments made by the plaintiff to external parties, with the accrual starting from the plaintiff's actual payment date; RMB 90,373,828 was the remaining amount after deducting the aforementioned two payments from the amounts payable by the two defendants, and for convenience of calculation, the interest loss was calculated from the date of the third-to-last payment made by the plaintiff to external parties, i.e., June 29, 2011.

The Shanghai Maritime Court held at first instance:

The plaintiff Zhonghai Industry and the two defendants all had no dispute that a valid construction insurance contract for a vessel under construction existed between the plaintiff and the defendant Tai Bao Yangzhou Company, that Tai Bao Yangzhou Company was the insurer, that the accident in question fell within the insured perils stipulated in the insurance contract, and that the losses, liabilities, and expenses caused by the accident fell within the scope of the insurer's liability. The main issues in dispute in this case were threefold: 1. whether the plaintiff could limit its liability for maritime claims with respect to the accident; 2. the determination of the amount of insurance compensation and interest losses; and 3. the method of bearing civil liability by the two defendants.

**Regarding whether the plaintiff Zhonghai Industry could limit its liability for maritime claims with respect to the accident.** Pursuant to the provisions of Chapter 11 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Maritime Code) concerning limitation of liability for maritime claims, the prerequisite for enjoying limitation of liability for maritime claims must satisfy both subjective and objective conditions: 1. The persons entitled to limit liability for maritime claims are the owners, operators, or charterers of a ship, and the ship must be a ship as defined in Article 3 of the Maritime Code, i.e., a seagoing ship or other mobile marine installation, excluding river vessels, ships used for military or governmental public service purposes, and small vessels of less than 20 gross tons; 2. The claims for compensation for losses caused by the accident must be maritime claims subject to limitation. The court held that, first, the vessel "An Min Shan" did not constitute a ship within the meaning of the Maritime Code. A ship as defined in Article 3 of the Maritime Code should refer to a ship in its complete sense, including those that have undergone ship registration, passed various technical tests, and obtained formal ship certificates and a ship name. However, a vessel under construction has not undergone formal registration, nor has it obtained a formal certificate from the competent authority. Although it may have certain navigational capabilities during the trial voyage stage, it remains in the stage of testing and inspecting the hull. Whether it can ultimately pass the tests and obtain formal ship status is uncertain. Therefore, a vessel under construction does not constitute a ship within the meaning of the Maritime Code, and the plaintiff cannot be considered the shipowner or ship operator as provided in Chapter 11 of the Maritime Code. Second, even if a vessel under construction could be recognized as a ship under Article 3 of the Maritime Code, claims for compensation for losses caused by such a vessel during a trial voyage are difficult to categorize as maritime claims subject to limitation under existing legal provisions. Article 207 of the Maritime Code lists four categories of maritime claims subject to limitation: (1) claims for personal injury or loss of or damage to property occurring on board or directly connected with the operation of the ship or with salvage operations, including damage to port works, basins, waterways, and navigational aids, and consequential losses arising therefrom; (2) claims for loss resulting from delay in delivery of cargo at sea or from delay in the arrival of passengers or their luggage; (3) claims for other losses resulting from infringement of non-contractual rights directly connected with the operation of the ship or salvage operations; (4) claims of a person other than the person liable for measures taken to avoid or reduce losses for which the person liable may limit his liability in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, and further losses caused by such measures. The circumstances in items (2) and (4) above are not relevant to this case. Items (1) and (3) specifically emphasize that the loss caused by the accident must be directly connected with the "operation of the ship." Such a provision is consistent with the legislative spirit of the limitation of liability for maritime claims system—to protect the shipping industry and reduce risks for shipping operators. However, at the time of the accident, the "An Min Shan" was a vessel under construction, had not obtained a formal ship certificate, and lacked operational qualifications. Its trial voyage operation was not an activity directly connected with "ship operation," but rather an activity related to "ship construction." Therefore, the losses caused by the accident in question did not fall within the circumstances provided in Article 207 of the Maritime Code. Since the claims for compensation for personal injury and property loss caused by the "An Min Shan" during its trial voyage were not maritime claims subject to limitation under Article 207 of the Maritime Code, the plaintiff could not limit its liability for compensation pursuant to Chapter 11 of the Maritime Code. In summary, the plaintiff's full payment of compensation to the relevant loss parties and victims after the accident was in compliance with legal provisions and was not improper. The two defendants' defense that the plaintiff failed to exercise the right to limit liability for maritime claims during external compensation, thereby harming the insurer's interests, lacked sufficient basis, and the court did not accept it.

**Regarding the determination of the amount of insurance compensation and interest losses.** In this case, the losses of the plaintiff Zhonghai Industry could be roughly divided into four categories based on the recipients of payments: First, expenses and compensation paid by the plaintiff for on-site rescue, salvage, losses of the stricken vessel, compensation for deceased persons, etc., totaling RMB 13,080,100. Both the plaintiff and the defendants had no objection to this portion. Second, ship repair costs for repairing the "An Min Shan" incurred by the plaintiff. The plaintiff claimed RMB 10,642,031, while the two defendants only recognized RMB 6,092,011. Subsequently, during the trial, the plaintiff expressed willingness to accept the amount claimed by the two defendants. The court confirmed that the repair cost for the "An Min Shan" was RMB 6,092,011. Third, losses from the cleanup, reconstruction, and operating delay of the damaged dock. Regarding this loss, the appraisal company entrusted by Tai Bao Yangzhou Company made a detailed assessment in its report. The plaintiff and the two defendants had no objection to the amount of loss determined in the appraisal conclusion, and the court accepted it. However, because the plaintiff admitted during the trial that the actual payments for dock reconstruction and dock facility pipeline reconstruction were lower than the amounts determined in the appraisal report, these two items should be based on the plaintiff's actual payment amounts. Accordingly, the total for this portion was RMB 264,540,197. Fourth, the appraisal fee incurred by the plaintiff for calculating the dock's operational delay loss. The plaintiff claimed RMB 1,300,000, which included the fees of two accounting firms separately retained by the plaintiff and Donghua Company. However, the plaintiff failed to provide valid evidence of the RMB 600,000 paid to Jiangsu Fuhua Certified Public Accountants. Therefore, the court only supported the appraisal fee of RMB 700,000 for which there was evidence, and did not support the remaining fees. The total of the above four categories of losses was RMB 284,412,308, which exceeded the total insured amount of RMB 280,000,000 stipulated in the insurance contract. Therefore, Tai Bao Yangzhou Company should compensate the plaintiff up to the total insured amount. After deducting the absolute deductible of RMB 100,000 stipulated in the insurance contract and the RMB 60,000,000 already paid by Tai Bao Yangzhou Company in advance, the amount that Tai Bao Yangzhou Company should further compensate the plaintiff was RMB 219,900,000. Regarding the interest losses claimed by the plaintiff, according to the insurance contract, Tai Bao Yangzhou Company should have paid indemnity to the plaintiff within four weeks after the accident. However, to date, Tai Bao Yangzhou Company has only paid RMB 60,000,000 to the plaintiff, while the plaintiff's actual external compensation amounted to RMB 284,412,308. The plaintiff's claim for interest losses was legally based and could be supported. According to the plaintiff's claims and its external payment situation, the interest loss on the insurance indemnity of RMB 219,900,000 could be calculated in three segments: RMB 73,240,000 from June 29, 2011, until the effective date of the judgment; RMB 141,969,500 from November 14, 2011, until the effective date of the judgment; and RMB 4,690,500 from January 9, 2012, until the effective date of the judgment. Regarding the standard for interest losses, the court held that the interest loss in this case could be calculated at the one-year deposit rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, as deemed appropriate.

**Regarding the method of bearing civil liability by the two defendants.** The plaintiff Zhonghai Industry requested that the two defendants bear joint and several liability. The court held that the plaintiff and the two defendants all recognized that the party contracting the insurance contract with the plaintiff was Tai Bao Yangzhou Company. Although Tai Bao Yangzhou Company did not have legal personality, it was a financial branch established according to law and holding a business license, with independent litigation subject status and external debt performance capability. It should bear civil compensation liability to the plaintiff as the insurer under the involved insurance contract. Tai Bao Company was not the insurer under the involved insurance contract and should not directly bear the compensation liability under the insurance contract. However, as the parent company of Tai Bao Yangzhou Company, Tai Bao Company should bear supplementary compensation liability for any insufficiency in Tai Bao Yangzhou Company's solvency.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 107 and Article 112 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 237 and Article 238 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai Maritime Court rendered the following judgment on March 6, 2012:

1. The defendant Tai Bao Yangzhou Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay to the plaintiff Zhonghai Industry insurance compensation of RMB 219,900,000 and interest losses on that amount (RMB 73,240,000 from June 29, 2011, until the effective date of the judgment; RMB 141,969,500 from November 14, 2011, until the effective date of the judgment; and RMB 4,690,500 from January 9, 2012, until the effective date of the judgment, all calculated at the one-year deposit rate of the People's Bank of China);

2. The defendant Tai Bao Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability for item 1;

3. The other claims of the plaintiff Zhonghai Industry are rejected.

After the first-instance judgment, none of the parties—plaintiff or defendants—filed an appeal, and the first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
